findings.failure_condition: C2-flow reopens FileAnalysisStore in a fresh Node process before replay, but asserts only the command detail output and item_key. It never compares the persisted command input against the independent fixture, nor checks conversation/turn/source metadata of the persisted ToolStarted/ToolCompleted history events. Command input or tool association can be lost on reopen while the 148/148 suite still passes; the verification report nevertheless claims command detail and source/turn were compared.
findings.required_behavior: In the inspect-only child before full replay, assert the persisted command input and output against independent fixture values and assert the command history events retain the expected conversation, turn, item key and source identity; keep the existing file and checkpoint checks.

test_assessment.applicability: C2-rule finding is resolved by the amended selector and 42/42 current-source run. C2-flow 148/148 passed as executed, but its persisted command and tool association claim is not established.
test_assessment.boundary: C2-rule executes vendored Rust decode through Adapter and owned projection; C2-flow executes real Node/Rust stdio and File stores, with inspect-only fresh Node child before full replay.
test_assessment.necessity: The real Node process and File store reopen test is necessary to detect persistence loss before a replay can reconstruct values; Rust unit/target tests cannot substitute for that boundary.
test_assessment.oracle: Rust rollout_blockers asserts exact command input/output and metadata, and the Node fixture supplies independent expected cargo test input, but reopened Node assertions omit tool input and tool event associations.
test_assessment.reason: Cumulative S3 review includes new persistent Rust and Node lifecycle tests and six final execution slots; the C2-flow oracle is incomplete at the reopened-store boundary.
test_assessment.reuse: The frozen C2-rule selector now includes the existing rollout_blockers target; C2-flow reuses the six-file Node suite and its lifecycle fixture, requiring only stronger assertions in the admitted test file.
